payload.name: Multimedia Principle
payload.fact: The multimedia principle, which suggests that people learn better from words and pictures than from words alone, produces a small positive significant effect on learning outcomes and can be transferred to educational testing material.
payload.boundary: Effectiveness of multimedia-based instruction is moderated by instructional setting, with smaller effects observed in P-12 settings compared to higher education; applicable to educational testing materials as well as general multimedia learning contexts.

provenance.title: Effects of Multimedia-based Education on Learning Outcomes: An Evidence Gap Map Analysis and A Second Order Meta-analysis
provenance.quote_or_locus: It was found that there was a small positive significant effect size of multimedia-based education on cognitive and affective learning outcomes

provenance.title: Effects of Multimedia-based Education on Learning Outcomes: An Evidence Gap Map Analysis and A Second Order Meta-analysis
provenance.quote_or_locus: Instructional setting was found to moderate the influence of multimedia-based education on learning, with the effect estimated in P-12 settings being smaller compared to the effect estimated in higher education

provenance.title: Representational and decorative pictures in science and mathematics tests: Do they make a difference?
provenance.quote_or_locus: The pattern of results indicates that the multimedia principle and the coherence principle from instructional psychology can be transferred to educational testing material
